title: SILMARILS-MV: Information-Theoretically Secure Multi-Verifier Signatures with Dealer-Free Key Issuance and Linear Aggregation for Permissioned Blockchains
authors: Khadijeh Bagheri, Hassan Khodaiemehr, Chen Feng
abstract: Permissioned blockchains authenticate transactions, votes and quorum certificates with computationally secure signatures, and post-quantum replacements inflate consensus traffic by orders of magnitude. Information-theoretic alternatives have required a trusted authority, quantum channels, per-signature interaction, or single-use keys with bounded transfer. We present SILMARILS-MV, a multi-verifier unconditionally secure signature in which a signature is the vector $α= A\,e(m)$ and each verifier holds a secret functional $c_i = Γ^T λ(x_i)$ derived from virtual anchors $Γ$ that nobody learns. Against unbounded adversaries corrupting up to $ω$ verifiers and any signers, and observing every decision, an honest verifier accepts a forged or invalid signature with probability at most $Q/q + 1/(q-1)$, a bound that is tight in its leading term. The scheme is strongly unforgeable, non-repudiable, transferable across unboundedly many hops, and linearly aggregatable. Keys are issued by the validators through perfectly secure MPC for $t < n/3$, without broadcast. To scale, we let the committee itself sign: in threshold notarization, finality certificates have constant size $32(ω+1)$ bytes and per-validator issuance cost no longer depends on $n$. Arbiter-verified keys give clients 32-byte signatures, robust redistribution supports membership changes and share refresh, and verifiers can be enrolled retroactively. A certificate verifies in 2.4 microseconds. In an analytic normal-case model at 1000 validators, threshold notarization needs 71 KiB of authentication traffic per validator per block, 22x less than ML-DSA-44 for admitted verifiers. In a Rust HotStuff prototype with 100 validators, SILMARILS-MV commits 2.8x more transactions per second than ML-DSA-44 with 67x less cryptographic CPU, and Monte-Carlo attacks match the bounds.
summary: This paper introduces SILMARILS-MV, a novel, unconditionally secure multi-verifier signature scheme designed for permissioned blockchains. It solves critical issues in current blockchain signatures by offering dealer-free key issuance and linear aggregation. The scheme demonstrates superior performance, requiring significantly less bandwidth and CPU power compared to established post-quantum alternatives.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for an information-theoretically secure, multi-verifier signature scheme for permissioned blockchains that overcomes limitations of existing methods regarding trust assumptions and scalability.
main_result: SILMARILS-MV provides an unconditionally secure signature that is strongly unforgeable, linearly aggregatable, and features constant-size finality certificates, significantly outperforming existing schemes in both bandwidth and computational efficiency.
method: The scheme constructs the signature as a vector $\alpha = A e(m)$ and relies on secret functional keys $c_i$ derived from virtual anchors $\Gamma$ to ensure unconditional security.
model_or_system: The model is a permissioned blockchain environment utilizing Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) protocols, involving a committee of validators and external verifiers.
key_observables: Verification time ($2.4 \mu s$), authentication traffic per validator per block ($71 \text{ KiB}$ at 1000 validators), and transaction throughput (2.8x more than ML-DSA-44 in a prototype).
important_parameters: The security relies on tolerating up to $\omega$ corrupt verifiers and requires the committee size $n$ to support $t < n/3$ for key issuance.
main_assumptions: The scheme assumes the existence of perfectly secure MPC for key issuance and operates within the context of BFT consensus mechanisms.
figures_summary: The notes mention tables comparing the scheme against prior work and summarizing its contributions across various cryptographic dimensions.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the SILMARILS-MV scheme using algebraic tools, proves its security properties, and concludes with performance evaluations and comparisons to state-of-the-art signatures like ML-DSA-44.
why_interesting: While purely cryptographic, the focus on achieving information-theoretic security and high efficiency for distributed ledger technology (DLT) has implications for secure quantum-resistant networking protocols.
